states.h1: Two clouds: OW climbed toward ODSP in every CMA
states.lead: From 2003 Q1 to 2026 Q1, the share of cases that are a single person without children rose in both programs across Ontario: OW 49.5% → 69.7%, ODSP 76.4% → 81.1%. The gap between the programs went from 26.9 to 11.4 percentage points. It was smaller at the end than at the start in all 15 CMAs: by the most in Oshawa (36.0 → 12.0), by the least in Ottawa–Gatineau (24.6 → 14.8).
states.story: Both shares rose; the gap was smaller at the end everywhere. Across Ontario the OW share rose +20.1 pp and the ODSP share +4.6 pp, so the gap went from 26.9 to 11.4 pp. The ODSP share was above the OW share in every CMA-quarter, so the gap never reversed. The opening at the top shows the same change for Ontario as 100 squares per program. In Figure 1a the blue cloud rises much more than the orange one, so the space between them shrinks from 20.1 pp (2003 Q1) to 4.0 pp (2026 Q1). The zipper with hollow markers is Ontario as a whole.
states.f1Title: Share of cases that are a single person without children, OW (blue) and ODSP (orange): every CMA, every year (first quarter), 2003–2026
states.f1Take: The clouds never overlap. In all 93 quarters the lowest ODSP share among the 15 CMAs was above the highest OW share. The space between the clouds went from 20.1 pp in 2003 Q1 to 4.0 pp in 2026 Q1, mostly because the OW cloud rose: the median CMA's OW share went from 47.9% to 69.3%, its ODSP share from 77.6% to 81.3%.
